comment: To the Members of the Salt Lake City Council and Mayor Mendenhall, Thank you for your thoughtful consideration of our application for CDBG funding in support of the English Skills Learning Center's ESL Job Readiness program for immigrant and refugee adults. This program is unique in it's design, curriculum, and outcomes. We focus our services on an adult population with extremely low-levels of English proficiency, limited or interrupted formal education, and sometimes, adults who have never learned to read or write in any language. Because of these adults' limited employability, we concentrate our efforts on providing the most urgent language and literacy skills needed to help them find and keep employment. This program is not duplicated by any other program in the valley, and has demonstrated continued and improved success over the 5-6 years it has been funded. We hope that we can count on your continued support to serve this challenged population next year. Thank you. Catherine Barnhart Executive Director

Dear Salt Lake City Council Members, I express my sincere appreciation for the work that each of you is doing to keep our city operating during the ongoing threat from Coronavirus, and heartfelt concern for Councilmember Darin Mano. You are in our thoughts and prayers. Under different circumstances, I would certainly prefer to share these comments with you in person. For the last 50 years, ASSIST Community Design Center has been leveraging architecture, planning, and construction to provide equitable housing and transportation choices for all communities. During that time our organization has played a critical role in promoting the development of our current public transportation systems, and has participated in the design development of dozens of facilities for community-based organizations. Most significantly, we have completed tens of thousands of home repairs and accessibility modifications throughout Salt Lake County these repairs have helped eliminate blight and stabilize neighborhoods, and have allowed vulnerable households to continue living in their homes and communities. In the past 20 years alone, and with the support of CDBG funding from Salt Lake City and other municipalities in the county, ASSIST has invested over $13.2 million in brick and mortar improvements for low-income households, at an average cost of approximately $1000.00 per job. The average income of all clients served during that time is just 32% of the area median income truly this program is making a significant impact in the lives of our most vulnerable residents. We are grateful for Mayor Mendenhall's recommendation for continued funding of ASSIST's programs for the upcoming fiscal year, and fully support the City's efforts to leverage CDBG funds to benefit those most in need. Sincerely, Jason Wheeler, AIA Executive Director ASSIST Inc COMMUNITY DESIGN CENTER www.assistutah.org

South Valley Services would like to thank the review committee, City Council and Mayor Mendenhall for recommending us for funding. 1 in 3 women and 1 in 4 men in Utah will experience domestic violence. 71% of those that we serve also have children in their household. Through these funds we will be able to empower men, women and children impacted by domestic violence to become self-sufficient and feel a sense of well-being. Many domestic survivors face the difficult choice between staying with or returning to their abusers or becoming homeless if they leave. South Valley Services provides opportunities and choices to help survivors feel safe and empowered. Thank you, Peggy Daniel Development Director South Valley Services/South Valley Sanctuary

Dear City Council Members We are grateful for the opportunity to submit an application, and it looks like we are in good company with those that were not funded. We would like for you to consider a few pieces of information about the work we do. We serve girls aging out (turning 18 years old) from Juvenile Justice Services who have been sexually exploited/trafficked, trafficked women, women fleeing domestic violence with criminal justice histories and women, LBGTQI+ and their safe partners transitioning from the Prison, the local Jails, and those experiencing Homelessness. Our mentoring program at the prison diverts hundreds of women leaving prison from the homeless shelters. We start working with these women 3-6 mo. prior to their release to ensure they have a safe place to live upon release, trauma informed treatment settings, livable wage employment and the best possible opportunity to be successful on parole. We have 17% recidivism in this program in 6 years, and the State rate is the highest in the country at 70%. We are doing our best with the resources we have to interrupt the sexual assault to prison pipleine in Utah. We are above the National Average in Sexual Assault, and Domestic Violence Homicide in this State. When victims are not allowed to survive as children, they turn to self medicating behaviors and end up filling up our criminal justice system. We have an opiate epidemic and a suicide epidemic in Utah because of the ACE (adverse childhood experiences) trauma experienced by children in our State. We can interrupt this pipeline! Harmed children do not have to end up filling out adult jails and our prison! We are an amazing resilient loving community, we can change these outcomes! We are the only evidence based Gender-Responsive Trauma-Responsive resource standing in the gap for these women, LBGTQI+, and these extremely vulnerable girls! We are keeping hundreds of women and girls from ending up in the homeless shelter pipeline. We would like for the city council to consider this effort when considering where the funding will go this year. Thank You for your Consideration, Shannon Miller Cox *This comment has corresponding material

Dear Salt Lake City Council, I want to express my gratitude to the Salt Lake City Council for your enduring commitment to assisting organizations like First Step House address the healthcare, housing and employment needs of vulnerable individuals in our community. We appreciate the thoughtful work of the Salt Lake City Citizens that comprise the CDBG Board and their recommendations in this process. We, at this time, ask that the Salt Lake City Council fund the requests made by First Step House at the levels recommended by Mayor Mendenhall for the following programs: First Step House Employment Preparation and Placement Program (CDBG) - $47,000 First Step House Peer Support Services (CDBG) - $50,000 First Step House Homeless Resource Center Behavioral Health Treatment Services (ESG) - $60,000 All three programs are currently supported by Salt Lake City and have had tremendous positive impact for people experiencing homelessness, substance use disorders, and mental health conditions in our community. Our SLC quarterly reports indicate that we are exceeding our projected number of people served due to the demand for these services in our community. We are also exceeding anticipated program outcomes in the areas of helping our target population achieve meaningful employment, increase income, successfully complete treatment, and exit to stable and permanent housing. At this time, we don't feel it necessary to make public comment this evening at the, modified format, Salt Lake City Council Meeting. I will join the WebEx Session and be available for any Members of the Council or Staff who have a question. Today and this evening, I can best be reached on my cell phone at: [REDACTED]. Please do not hesitate to reach out for additional information. We appreciate SLC's continued support and your commitment to bettering our community. Most respectfully, Shawn M. McMillen, MPA, ASUDC Executive Director First Step House [REDACTED]
